subject.title: [Feature]: Optimization for Dockerfile.sandbox-common # add retries and fix-missings for apt-get

question: Should sandbox Dockerfile builds use retry-only APT resilience, or should OpenClaw intentionally accept `--fix-missing` partial-install semantics with package verification?
rationale: Current main lacks the requested retry behavior, but the linked implementation also changes package-install failure semantics; automation should not decide that build contract for maintainers.

options.title: Retry-only APT resilience
options.body: Keep `Acquire::Retries=5`, remove `--fix-missing`, and require build plus package-presence proof before merging the linked PR or a replacement.

options.title: Accept partial-install semantics
options.body: Keep `--fix-missing` only if maintainers explicitly want that contract and add verification that required tools are present in the final images.

options.title: Decline the Dockerfile change
options.body: Close the issue and linked PR if maintainers decide transient package mirror handling should remain outside these source-checkout sandbox Dockerfiles.

recommendation.title: Retry-only APT resilience
recommendation.body: Keep `Acquire::Retries=5`, remove `--fix-missing`, and require build plus package-presence proof before merging the linked PR or a replacement.
